data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Hutamah means 'seal' or 'stamp'. It is a name of noble origin in Islamic history, as it was the name of a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and a leader in the early Muslim community. The name Hutamah carries the meaning “Seal, Stamp” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hutamah usually hope their child will grow to embody seal, stamp and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Additionally, the name has been passed down through generations and continues to be used among Muslim communities, reflecting the rich history and traditions of the Islamic faith.
